title: 2026-11-05_Adwind_jRAT_Incident_Response_bf6
description: Investigate a compromised host infected with the Adwind/jRAT trojan, identify malicious activities, understand the infection vector, and contain the threat.
outcomes: Enumerate running and inactive services to identify suspicious activities.
Investigate systemd service configurations to discover persistence mechanisms.
Analyze network communication to identify command and control (C2) activities.
Preserve forensic evidence and contain the threat.

levels.title: Scenario Overview
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised host infected with the Adwind/jRAT trojan. This cross-platform remote access trojan (RAT) is capable of stealing credentials, recording keystrokes, taking screenshots, and exfiltrating data. Your mission is to identify the malicious activities, understand the infection vector, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Access Information
levels.cloud_content: Access the victim host (IP: 192.168.60.10) via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: SecurePass123.
levels.local_content: Access the victim host (IP: 192.168.60.10) via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: SecurePass123.

levels.title: Identify the Credential Harvester Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity of periodically collecting `/etc/passwd`, home directory listings, and sensitive files, then exfiltrating them to a C2 server.
levels.solution:
1. Enumerate Running Services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
Look for unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

2. Inspect Service Details:
```bash
systemctl cat net-diag-harvest.service
```
Examine the service configuration for suspicious ExecStart paths or descriptions.

3. Check Service Status:
```bash
systemctl status net-diag-harvest.service
```
Verify if the service is active and running.

4. Identify the Service Name:
The service responsible for the suspicious activity is `net-diag-harvest.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service configuration.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port for Exfiltration
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system for exfiltrating data to a C2 server. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the Service Configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat net-diag-harvest.service
```
Look for the ExecStart path, which contains the script launched by the service.

2. Examine the Script:
```bash
cat /usr/local/lib/.netd/harvester.sh
```
Identify the port number used for communication with the C2 server.

3. Verify the Port:
The port number used for exfiltration is `1033`.

hints.content: Use `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the ExecStart path in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Examine the script at the specified path to find the port number.

levels.title: Identify the Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the Credential Harvester Service running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List All Timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
Look for timers associated with the suspicious service.

2. Inspect the Timer Configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat net-diag-harvest.timer
```
Examine the timer configuration for details about its activation.

3. Check Timer Status:
```bash
systemctl status net-diag-harvest.timer
```
Verify if the timer is active and running.

4. Identify the Timer Name:
The timer responsible for the persistence of the Credential Harvester Service is `net-diag-harvest.timer`.
